conclusion: The push happens on `yes` and on nothing else. `y`, `n` and an absent terminal are all refusals: after each, every ref on the remote points at the same object it did before -- checked by name AND by object, because comparing names alone would pass a run that rewrote `trunk`. Each case's exit status is checked too, so a crash cannot be recorded as a refusal correctly honoured. The approved push carries one commit touching only the file the migration wrote.

cases.why_it_matters: A CI job, a pipe or a nohup has nobody in it to say no. Fail-closed is the only safe reading of silence when the action is a push.
